drawings.description: en haut à droite de la page : deux segments côte à côte, le premier étiqueté « $E_p$ » (avec une accolade), portant un gros point marqué $\alpha$, le second, épais, étiqueté « $E'_q$ » (avec une accolade) ; au-dessous, entre les deux, la mention « $E \setminus \{\alpha\}$ » précédée d'une accolade.
drawings.kind: two segments E_p and E'_q, a marked point alpha (the surjection (**))
drawings.notes: As on the page: the first segment with its end marks, the heavy point on it (computed on the segment) and the letter alpha below; the second segment, heavy, with its end marks; above each its label after a brace (E_p, E'_q); below, the brace and the legend E minus {alpha}. Nothing struck. Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour facsimile on 2026-11-12 (Opus 5.5): the segments, marks, point and labels lie on the page within about 1 mm; not changed. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: au bas de la page, au milieu, quatre figures griffonnées, sans lettres. À gauche : trois points entourés d'un ovale (les deux premiers encadrés), trois autres points au-dessous entourés d'un second ovale, et trois boucles étroites obliques joignant ceux du haut à ceux du bas. À droite : deux points encadrés et un troisième à côté, le tout entouré d'un ovale ; au-dessous, deux points entourés d'un ovale. Plus bas : un segment épais à deux points marqués, dont la partie droite est encadrée.
drawings.kind: scribbled figures: marked points grouped by ovals and frames (count of fixed points)
drawings.notes: Right: a frame round two points and a third point beside it, all three inside an oval; below, two points inside an oval. Bottom: a heavy segment with two marked points, a frame round its right part (the right point is inside the frame). Left: three points in an oval, a frame round the first two; three points below in a second oval; three narrow oblique loops (spindles) from above the upper row down to the lower row. Still differs: the left figure is scribbled over itself; which points each narrow loop contains is a reading (drawn as the page shows them: the first round the second upper point and the first lower point, the second round the third upper point and the second lower point, the third, at the right, ending at the third lower point); a long stroke from the top left of the upper oval down to its lower left, and the strokes crossing the two ovals, are left out as scribbling. Not redrawn: the zigzag pen trial lower on the page (no content). Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour facsimile on 2026-11-12 (Opus 5.5) and corrected: the three narrow loops were single strokes and are now drawn as the narrow closed loops of the page, each from its own outline; the two ovals of the left figure refitted (0.5 to 1 mm). The right-hand figures and the segment with its frame lie on the page within 1 mm. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again. 2026-11-13, Claude Opus 5.5, overlay check (issue 147): laid over the scan rendered at 400 dpi in colour, whole and zoomed on the left figure (26 px a unit); not compiled (no TeX engine in the session), the TikZ was rasterised by a script; nothing changed. The right-hand figures, the segment with its frame, the points, the frames and the three spindles lie on their ink within about 1 unit. Kept partial for the left figure: its two « ovals » are drawn as ellipses, while on the page each is a free loop gone round more than once, open where the pen started (the upper one has a spiral of two or three turns and a hooked start at the top left), so the ellipses leave the ink by 1 to 3 units in places; the long stroke down the left side and the strokes crossing the two ovals are still left out as scribbling.

figures.what: two rows of three points joined by loops

drawings.description: en marge gauche, un dessin : un cercle coupé en deux arcs $A$ (à gauche) et $B$ (à droite) par deux points marqués $a$ (en bas) et $b$ (en haut), et le cône de sommet $o$ tracé sur ce cercle : deux génératrices tangentes au contour et les deux génératrices $oa$ et $ob$.
drawings.kind: circle cut into two arcs A, B by two points, and the cone of vertex o over it
drawings.notes: The circle (an ellipse fitted to his outline) with the two marked points on it, b at the top and a at the bottom, the letters A and B beside the left and right arcs; the vertex o below at the left; four lines from o, all drawn from the one vertex: the two outer ones, the left one stopping short of the outline and the right one reaching it at the lower right; the generator towards a, drawn from o two thirds of the way and stopping (the small mark in the gap is the letter a); the generator towards b, full from o for a third of its length, then dashed up to the circle, then, inside the disc, a full stroke ending at b (the inner stroke is not quite in line with the dashes: drawn as on the page). The small letters beside the two points are barely legible: read b (top) and a (bottom) after the note of the transcription. Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour facsimile on 2026-11-12 (Opus 5.5) and corrected: the points a and b stood 3 mm below their places and the circle 1.5 mm low; the circle refitted, a and b put on the heavy blots of the outline, the generators redrawn as the page draws them (see above; the earlier redraw had them both full and had the broken one the wrong way round), the labels moved onto his letters. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: marge gauche, en bas, pris dans les lignes écrites en diagonale : un petit croquis à main levée --- un gros point traversé d'un trait épais, d'où partent vers la droite deux traits courbes fins finissant en flèche devant « $R_{ij}$ » ; au-dessous à droite, une seconde tache d'où une flèche remonte vers le gros point, avec « $X_i$ » dessous.
drawings.kind: small free-hand sketch among diagonal writing: a marked point with arrows, labels R_ij, X_i
drawings.notes: A heavy point with a short heavy stroke across it and a thin stroke to its left; two thin curved strokes to the right, one from the point and one from the upper end of the heavy stroke, crossing each other and meeting in an arrowhead before the label R_ij; a second heavy blot below at the right, and an arrow coming up to the first point from the lower right, with the label X_i under it (the transcription reads X_i^* among the labels of this sketch). Decided here, on the page: the three long wavy oblique strokes that run through the place are lines of the marginal NB written in diagonal (his fast hand reduces words to wavy strokes; each ends in a legible word or symbol), not parts of the sketch; they are left out, with the rest of the writing. Left out as well: two small letters beside the heavy point (not read). Still differs: the sketch cannot be separated with certainty from the handwriting that crosses it. The label C_ij named by the note of the transcription was not found in the sketch (the word « cylindre » stands at its right). Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour facsimile on 2026-11-12 (Opus 5.5) and corrected: the upper of the two thin curves leaves the upper end of the heavy stroke, not the point, and crosses the lower one; both redrawn from the page, the label R_ij moved onto his letters. The other strokes lie on the page within 1 mm. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again. 2026-11-13, Claude Opus 5.5, overlay check (issue 147): laid over the scan rendered at 400 dpi in colour, whole and zoomed (20-30 px a unit); not compiled (no TeX engine in the session), the TikZ was rasterised by a script. The two thin curves were re-read at 30 px a unit (they lay up to 2 units off): the one from the upper end of the heavy stroke runs down across the other to the lower of the two arrowheads before R_ij, the one from the heavy point rises to the upper one; both are now drawn ending in their heads. The heavy point, the heavy stroke, the second blot, the arrow up from X_i and the labels lie on their ink within about 1 unit. Left out as before: the diagonal lines of writing that cross the place and the two small letters beside the heavy point (not read). Which strokes are the sketch and which the writing is decided as above; the strokes drawn are those that belong to neither line of writing.
